proposed_widenings.name: item-attached flight with controller range and load-conditioned speed
proposed_widenings.justification: The existing magic-item activation family can target an item, but it cannot honestly express that the carpet itself becomes a flying subject, obeys directions only while its user is within 30 feet, and changes speed based on carried weight.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "You can make this carpet hover and fly by taking a Magic action ... It moves according to your directions if you are within 30 feet of it."

proposed_widenings.name: conditional speed tier keyed by carried load
proposed_widenings.justification: The current surface can grant a fixed speed, but it has no way to encode that the carpet's Fly Speed is halved when load exceeds normal capacity while remaining within the doubled maximum load.
proposed_widenings.evidence: "A carpet can carry up to twice the weight shown on the table, but its Fly Speed is halved if it carries more than its normal capacity."

notes: MagicItemRecord plus activation family is the right top-level fit, and the four carpet sizes could be modeled as record variants if the movement payload existed. I did not author content files because any current encoding would misstate the moving subject or omit the core remote-control/load mechanics.
